what_this_file_is: THE DECLARED EDGE LIST FOR THE LOGS. logs/ is scratch (see DECISION_logs_are_scratch.md), so a log edge needs no root outside the tree -- but it DOES need a declared coordinate, and an edge that is neither migrated nor declared is the mixed state this project rejects. `edges` is every place in the tree that still constructs a log path, each with a status and an anchor string; `migrated` is every edge that was re-pointed at cabinet_root.log_dir()/log_for(). test_declared_root.py section 7 FAILS if a new file starts constructing a log path, or if a declared anchor disappears, or if a 'migrated' file has started constructing one again. A list of edges that nothing checks is a resolution, not a mechanism.

edges.what: log_dir()/log_path() (the ONE destination) and log_for(bundle) (the admissible journal PER BUNDLE). Also LEGACY_CAPTURES, the nine captures declared in place because the ignore rule named an extension and they were committed before it named the directory.
constructs a logs path ON PURPOSE: it asserts that a file under logs/ is NOT in the declared domain, which is what keeps the record's sweeps out of scratch. A probe is not an edge.

writes <workdir>/logs/<UNIT>.out. The directory is an ARGUMENT ($2 <workdir>), not a derivation from the script's own location, so there is nothing to re-point: what this edge needed was the ignore rule, and it landed (.gitignore ignores logs/ whole, so a capture can no longer be staged by git add -A). Kept in this list because it is the live source of the .out captures that ARE tracked.
